caveats: CPU and heap profiling change absolute workload timings. Use profiles for attribution within their own diagnostic batches, not as replacements for the frozen unprofiled benchmark.
Phase instrumentation adds performance.now and counting overhead. Phase measurements indicate cost locations but are not causal proof or final acceptance timings.
Heap sampling estimates allocation, including allocations collected later. Sampled bytes and end-minus-start heap size do not measure retained memory or garbage-collection pause durations.
CPU profiles contain GC-category samples, but these data do not establish that additional GC time causes the main-to-preview gap; no forced-GC or dedicated GC trace control was recorded.
Inclusive heap category roots can overlap and must not be summed. Self categories and mapped frames have different attribution boundaries.

Exploratory runs are three-round local screens with fresh contexts, no separate discarded warmup and no forced-GC control; retain every valid sample. Compare paired variants within each batch, not absolute totals across batches.
No-scan removes required prepatch identity validation and is diagnosis only, never a shippable fix.
Bundle size and retained cold authoring code do not demonstrate an executable hot-path cause.
Publication remains held. This diagnostic summary does not authorize main/preview integration or publication.
